prompt.zh-TW: 小山咖啡上個月底的現金是 {{money:vars.cashBefore}}，這個月底變成 {{money:vars.cashAfter}}，但這個月的本期淨利幾乎是零。最可能發生了哪一類交易？
prompt.en: Hillside Coffee had {{money:vars.cashBefore}} in cash at the end of last month and {{money:vars.cashAfter}} at the end of this month, yet this month’s profit was close to zero. What kind of transaction most likely happened?

text.zh-TW: 店借了錢或股東增資，所以現金變多但沒有賺到
text.en: The shop borrowed money or the owner put in more capital, so cash rose without any profit

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。借款與增資都會讓現金增加，卻不會出現在損益表上。
feedback.en: Correct. Borrowing and new capital both raise cash without appearing on the income statement.

text.en: The shop made a large profit this month

feedback.zh-TW: 現金變多確實常常是賺錢的結果，這個直覺不壞。不過題目說本期淨利幾乎是零，所以這筆現金不是賺來的。
feedback.en: Cash often rises because of profit, so that instinct is reasonable. But the question says profit was close to zero, so this cash was not earned.

text.zh-TW: 店用現金買了一台新設備
text.en: The shop bought new equipment with cash

feedback.zh-TW: 買設備是付出現金，會讓現金變少，方向剛好相反。
feedback.en: Buying equipment pays cash out, so cash would fall, which is the opposite direction.

explanation.zh-TW: 現金變多卻沒有利益，表示錢不是賺來的，而是借來的或股東出的，所以是{{option:o_4qhs}}。{{option:o_3605}}把現金和利益畫上等號；{{option:o_envn}}的方向相反。學會從數字倒推，就能用報表看出公司做過什麼。
explanation.en: Cash rising without profit means the money was not earned; it was borrowed or contributed, so {{option:o_4qhs}} is right. {{option:o_3605}} equates cash with profit, and {{option:o_envn}} points the wrong way. Reasoning backwards from the figures is how you read what a company has done.
